content.label: This is great app to help in the aid in completing any daily tasks you may need to complete. It would be great if the app could go past 2 pages for daily tasks/reminders & some of the notifications could be a little bit louder.

Use on a daily basis

Shame widget is rather pointless given it has no interaction. Somewhat odd a backward step

It’s really simple and easy to use. Only thing I’d like to see improved is counting partially met goals e.g. say my goal is to drink 3L of water daily. If I drink 2.5L I’ve not met the goal for the day, fair enough, but it would be useful to demonstrate this in the charts somewhere.
Terrible app not intuitive to use at all. Wish I could get my money back. Not worth 4.99 waste of money

I’m currently tracking how much money I’m saving by cycling to work. Streaks helps me monitor my working week, shows data in an easily calculated calendar display. 
Easily track vitamin routines and super handy for medication schedules. 
Easily reminds and incentivises positive daily routines with a simplistic yet highly customisable UI. 
Consistent communication patterns also develop easy with a streaks set up. 
Using streaks quickly becomes a valuable tool in productivity and organisational abilities.

Has been very useful in getting some good habits up and running whilst limiting some bad ones! A few potential improvements for me would be...clicking a habit takes you directly to a related app of your choice, for example if your habit is to record calories daily then it should be possibly to click that habit and it take you into MyFitnessPal to complete it. Also I’d like to have more habits on one page rather have to keep switching.

Nothing even close to negative to say about this app, it has put my life totally back on track. That may sound sad but it's true, it's miraculous what a little star with a rising number can do when it's next to a habit you're trying to improve on.

Simple to use, about four billion theme options so the right colour hits you in the feels when it's time to clock in on your particular habit and an interface which sends a crisp high five to those little OCD sections of your brain each time you succeed.

Solid performance, works seamlessly with Apple Watch and costs much less than the sinking feeling of failure you get when you let your plans go to the wall each night.

If I could make one change, it'd be the ability to check the habits lined up for tomorrow, but without that it's still a thing of beauty.
Does all the basic habit stuff well and is nicely designed 👍

I really love this app and it’s helped me keep a track of if I’ve done things like taking my medication and also work towards self-improvement, especially as an autistic individual. My only complaint is that you can only have 12 tasks. Since I paid for the app, I don’t think this limit is fair. I understand that each page can only have 6 because of fitting the icons on the screen, but there should be more than just 2 pages. I’d like to be able to compartmentalise my tasks between ‘must do’, ‘should do’ and ‘could do’ - e.g. brushing my teeth, emptying my bins once a week, working out several times a week.
Best streak app

The app has a clean look which I like but it doesn’t do much to show you your streaks. 

I wanted the app so that I could stay motivated to achieve my habits by having a visual streak that I don’t want to break, but this app makes it hard for you to see the actual streak and as a result I find it as more of a gimmick than a useful habit tracker.

Great aesthetics and branding, not so good functionality!
Very clean and simple.

I found this at just the right time. I tried it a while ago but didn’t really get into it. Now, combined with a genuine desire to create better habits, this app is really coming into its own. The only thing which I would like to see done differently is I would like an option to have more than 12 on the go at one time. This may be controversial, and I can see the reasons behind having only 12. So, perhaps a compromise add functionality without tempting the user to create too many habits at once could be the ability to group clusters of related habits together. For example, I am trying to develop a reading habit for both fiction and non-fiction and so I have both of these as habits to track. If I could, for example, click on “reading“ and have two connected habits open up as options, that would be really cool. At the moment, one can create clusters of habits by, for example, calling the habit “read fiction, read non-fiction“ and just putting the habit as two sessions per day, but that is crude and unwieldy and doesn’t show if you missed one and not the other. Habit clusters would be awesome. Anyway, that would be the improvement I would really like to see, and that would make the tracker even more useful than it already is.
I can't even count the number of times when I had ahaaaa, wow moments with this app. Everytime i think "I wish this app had this functionality..." - there it is! Really impressive ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️💫

On the whole, it does what it says on the tin. Would have given 5 stars but has a bug for tasks that have to be completed more than once each day. Sometimes when I go to register the first occasion that day I have done that task, it won’t log that first time on its own,  but instead marks all the tasks as being completed for the whole day - which is a bit annoying.

The app looks great, but for a paid app it massively fails to deliver in terms of functionality and is simply the equivalent of making a tick on a calendar that you’ve either done something that day or not. 

What I’m missing, and hence the score, is a means in which to explore the habits i.e. are there any patterns anywhere etc. A great example of this is Daylio for mood tracking. 

I’ll continue to use the app for another month or so but cannot recommend it to anyone given that there are free apps out there with 10 times the functionality.

The app has a clean and mostly straight forward interface, which is often made confusing by multiple taps on an icon revealing loads of different metrics I didn’t need. I use the app daily and update it regularly, it has been an essential reminder for my tasks throughout the day - my main gripe is that regardless of whether I’ve marked something as complete, I’ll receive a reminder later in the day, multiple times, to tell me to do it. 

‘Work our for 20 minutes:
 Task completed: Work out for 20 minutes’

An hour later:
‘Don’t forget/miss Work our for 20 minutes to continue your streak’

I already did it! And marked it as such!
This app is awful!

This is a really great app, I love that it’s much more intuitive than other habit apps I’ve tried. I’ve found that most others you have to set a time to be notified, and I’ve never found that helpful as I start to expect it so get into the habit of ignoring it, whereas because this app decides when to notify me it feels like a genuine reminder.  Such a simple thing, yet so important. I like how customisable it is too, with all of the different icons, and how it integrates with my Apple Watch. I also appreciate that it’s a one time payment only, as I refuse to purchase subscriptions as it’s a rip off. 

The only downside to the app for me is that I expected it to be a little more goals oriented, which is probably just my misunderstanding but it is a small disappointment. I thought I’d be able to use it to plan out and track my progress towards large goals, but it’s basically a habit tracker.

content.label: Add end/due date better ui for settings editing etc.. great app

Overall an excellent app, but the customisation options should have been improved more than they have over time...

1. Option to see upto all 12 streaks on one screen

2. More colour/background options such as introducing some wallpapers

God Bless 🙂❤️🕊

I love this app. It allows me to hold myself to account to improve my habits.

Given what is happening with Covid 19, it’s great to be able to track and remind of routine hand washing !

Buggy app especially with syncing with iPad, but great concept.

Update: just doesn’t work
Works well on apple watch

I bought Streaks years ago but wasn’t particularly enamoured by it. I thought “why would I need another to do list?” So I promptly deleted the app and told myself off for buying it. 

It wasn’t until a good few years later after reading Atomic Habits that I went back to it as a habit tracker. It’s very powerful and helpful for this and I would highly recommend reading that book first then using the app. It really goes hand in hand and makes so much sense now. I’m achieving new habits and I’m noticing the positive changes that come with it. Today the app congratulated me for doing meditation each morning and even suggested I add another minute to achieve even better results! Great stuff.

title.label: Good app but could be better...

content.label: .. allow further customisation and have all habits on one screen. This must be fairly simple to implement. Having it across two screens is not user friendly. I would like to see all 12 habits in one look not have to switch between two lots of 6.

This app gives you a straightforward and simple way to track your progress on habit building. Made reading daily much easier and had given me another incentive to want to read. Seeing the streak number go up is rewarding and motivating to keep going. 

However, warning: this does not immediately make you more productive. It is merely a way to see your progress and a reminder on what you want to make a habit. 

In my opinion, adding 6 streaks straight off the bat is a bad idea. It will be almost impossible, as i figured out myself, to start 6 streaks in one go. It is far better to start one or two streaks and add more as the initial streaks become engrained into your day to day life.

Just started with Streaks but it feels like a game-changer, having tried several similar apps in the past.  I love the integration into Apple Health to tie in with steps, mindfulness, sleep, calories etc. The automatic habits just seem to bring everything together, and it makes the whole process feel much more achievable. 

The interface is smart, the Apple Watch app works really well, and using the bundle app (Health Face) has been great for showing up my remaining calories on the Apple Watch too.

Great work, and so much better having a fair single purchase price than all these premium subscriptions, great decision by the developers.

Great utility to keep track of habits and goals. Flexible, easy to use and many health related habits can be tracked automagically from data inputted into other apps like myfitnesspal or lose it. Even integrates with the Apple Watch to bring across data like move goal tracking and much more.
Hello there, I would like to amend my goals, please assist me with a solution. Thank you.

title.label: Absolute amazing but missing one thing

content.label:
This app is truly amazing. I can literally sit here and write how much it helped me organise my days but following up on my habits. I’ve managed to get rid of many bad habits and implemented good ones.

The only thing missing is that I wish you could set a goal. For example, you’d set a goal of 100 days for the task (or habit) and each day you complete it tells you 1/100, 30/100 etc.
I think this allows the person to wanna stick to the task even more when they see their goal.

I payed £6 and the max limit is 12 tasks! 

Do not buy, very disappointing!

The app is simple yet very useful. Works great across my iPhone and iPad. I picked it up because it’s a one time purchase, while most competitors require an annual subscription. I’m very happy with my choice.
Changed my life!

title.label: Clear and easy to set up and track

content.label: Really like this app, especially the integrations - would like to see more of those with other apps. Best tracking app I’ve used, not too complicated and customisable

What can I say. Just AMAZING!

I am blown away with what can be done with this great app;  both in life and with the app functions.

Perfect with the Apple Watch. 

If you are thinking about getting it, stop thinking. Just get it!!!!

Get yourself into positive habits with this app supporting you. You can set as many challenges as you want for either pre selected or fully individual activities. Get a 'tick' when you complete it.... It's a star reward chart for adults.....works for me!!
You can choose what you want to record and keep the full history for the whole year. I love it!

content.label: Using mainly for diet/exercise - would be great if they could link with monzo so you could set spend limit/no spend streaks

title.label: Great but needs a little more...

content.label: This app is amazingly simple to use and for me, making sure the streaks aren’t broken, really makes me want to achieve the tasks set. The app really deserves 5 stars but I am taking a star off because I find having the ability to have only two pages (12 tasks) limiting. The developers have addressed this by stating that it wouldn’t be wise to set too many tasks for them to be achieved but I think that’s really a call the user should make. At the very least, there should be 3 pages so that the user can split tasks into morning, daytime and evening or perhaps daily, weekly and monthly. It is a great app though so I definitely do not regret the purchase but I do hope the developers consider and add page function going forward.
Good to get more of a committed timetable going when you are juggling lots of things
Like most things, the simpler they are the more effective they tend to be. Streaks fits that bill and proof is that you keep using it to track what ever you need. Great app.

title.label: Almost there but just needs to be ubiquitous with other apps

content.label:
Add more sync options to automatically update study and reading data to third party apps and this is a complete winner!

Examples like Audible/Apple Books app, Duolingo, and educational apps like DataCamp, Udemy, etc.

Simple, easy to use and has a nice and minimal style. I’ve tried a lot of these kinds of apps recently, but most lock features away or overcomplicate themselves just to try and justify locking you into a subscription (which seems quite ridiculous for what are basically glorified ‘To Do’ lists). 

Finally something you can pay for once and then just use.
It’s not as good as its described waste of money

This app has helped me manage goals and develop new habits. The design is bold and simple, I can keep track of completions really easily, and it helps me realise when a goal is unrealistic or needs to be set a bit higher.

Really can’t recommend it enough. Helping me make so many positive changes to my life.

This does help a bit when trying to form better habits, it is a good idea and has a nice simple interface. I feel it might have been better with more customisation and maybe the ability to add more tasks. As an example the application is always asking me to do a task I have set to twice a month, but this is unhelpful because the particular task needs doing at the beginning and end of the month.
I have given up with one task as it seemed to break my streak even though I met the two failure goal (I think it is because I had to go back to update that I passed the task). The timer feature is completely useless. My device turns off because it is idle and after that it fails to time correctly. Sometimes i need to pause the task and restart it, others I open the app again and it still says I have just started the task, and the timer starts going down but a bit quicker to make up for the error. I raised a bug back in January but it still seems broken.

It’s a great app for tracking your habit. I really liked the way it uses your health data.

My only criticism is the limit for habits. I needed to add more than 12 habits. You should find a way to let us add more habits than 12. Please consider this on the next update.
Amazing app. Changing my life. Would love to have more than 12 tasks please !
I can’t work out how to use this thing. I can’t find the tutorial. It’s really not intuitive.
Genuinely the best app I have.
